rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Shuʿayb was Moses’ father-in-law, the account of Moses naturally follows the preceding account of Shuʿayb and earlier allusions to scripture and the staff-miracle.
rows.anchor: ولما كان شعيب ختن موسى عليهما السلام , كان ذكر قصته هنا متوقعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic opening signals that Pharaoh acted like Quraysh in turning away from great signs, and Moses omitted none of the warning revealed to him.
rows.anchor: تنبيها على أن فرعون فعل فعل قريش في الإدبار عن الآيات العظيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs are the miracles Moses displayed.
rows.anchor: بآياتنا } أي المعجزات التي أظهرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The manifest authority means a compelling power over the Copts; al-Biqāʿī thinks this is probably Moses describing Pharaoh’s force and hostility toward him.
rows.anchor: أي أمر قاهر للقبط , والظاهر أنه حكاية موسى عليه السلام منه على ما كان له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Āyah can mean either a sign or decisive proof, sulṭān is specifically decisive proof, and mubīn denotes something manifest or clarifying.
rows.anchor: والآية تعم الأمارة والدليل القلاطع , و السلطان يخص القاطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh is the tyrant of the Copts; the chiefs are the nobles followed by the common people, and the main purpose was to free the Israelites from their control.
rows.anchor: إلى فرعون } طاغية القبط { وملئه } أي أشراف قومه الذين تتبعهم الأذناب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chiefs followed Pharaoh’s wishes and commands, then the lower people followed them, so nearly all opposed Moses except those God willed otherwise.
rows.anchor: فتسبب عن هذا الأمر الباهر أن عصى فرعون وحمل ملؤه أنفسهم على أن تبعوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following is the second party’s taking the first party’s conduct as its own, possibly unwillingly; a command can express general intent without requiring literal compliance, and rashīd means guiding to good.
rows.anchor: والإتباعن طلب , طلب الثاني للتصرف بتصرف الأول في أي جهة أخذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Pharaoh’s command unrighteous recalls the signs given to Thamūd and Moses and the surah’s reminder of resurrection, which should make people fear God and pursue good; al-Biqāʿī also links Abraham’s story after Ṣāliḥ’s.
rows.anchor: مع أن في هذا التعقيب بعد ذكر ثمود من التذكير بآياتي الناقة والعصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These narratives chiefly strengthen the Messenger to deliver the warning despite hostility, rejection, few followers, or uncertainty about the audience’s response.
rows.anchor: التثبيت في المكافحة بإبلاغ الإنذار وإن اشتدت كراهية المبلغين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelites initially hesitated only from fear of Pharaoh, then all followed; later defections arose from other causes, not aversion to the warning.
rows.anchor: فإنهم لم يتوقفوا إلا خوفا من فرعون في أول المر , ثم أطبق كلهم على الإتباع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh will lead his people at the Resurrection as he led them in worldly life, with them following behind him.
rows.anchor: يقدم قومه } أي الذين كان لهم قوة المدافعة { يوم القيامة } ويكونون له تبعا كما كانوا في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past-tense wording for his future leading indicates that the event is as certain as something already completed.
rows.anchor: واشار بإيراد ما حقه المضارع ماضيا إلى تحقق وقوعه تحقق ما وقع ومضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As Pharaoh brought his people to the sea in this life, he will bring them to the Fire in the next.
rows.anchor: اي كما أوردهم في الدنيا غطاءها وهو البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fire is the worst destination: a watering place should relieve thirst and cool the heart, whereas this destination does the opposite.
rows.anchor: لأن الورد يراد لتسكين العطش وتبريدالأكباد , وهذا يفيد ضد ذاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive form of being followed by a curse emphasizes the deed rather than identifying a particular agent; this life is contemptible.
rows.anchor: ببنائه للمفعول لأن المنكي الفعل لا كونه من معين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are cursed in this life by Muslims and members of other religious communities, and cursed again on the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: فهم يلعنون يها من كل لاعن من المسلمين وغيرهم من أهل الملل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their curse in this life and the next, with punishment accompanying both, is a wretched succession of support and recompense.
rows.anchor: اي التبع المتبوع والعون المعان , فإن اللعنة تابعة لعذابهم في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaqdum means Pharaoh is ahead rather than driving them; they follow close behind and enter the Fire together, while laʿn means God’s judgment of exclusion from mercy or people’s prayer for that exclusion.
rows.anchor: أنه يكون قدامهم غير سائق لهم , بل هم على أثره متلاحقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding threat rests on God’s knowledge and power: He alone knows all that is unseen in the heavens and earth, including what people wrongly imagine outside His power.
rows.anchor: أي المحيط وحده بكل شيءموات والأرض } أي جميع ما غاب علمه عن العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God created people and their capacities for disagreement, the threat might seem to imply acts against His will; the answer is that outward and inward affairs alike belong to Him.
rows.anchor: وكان تهديدهم على المعاصي ربما أوهم أنه بغير إرادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All affairs return to God, both now in obscurity and ultimately in clarity; this comprehends knowledge and power and means He will recompense good and evil.
rows.anchor: والرجوع : ذهاب الشيء إلى حيث ابتدأ منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The return of all affairs to God entails worshipping Him alone and relying on Him in every matter because He is strong and firm.
rows.anchor: { فاعبده } أي وحده عبادة لا شوب فيها { وتوكل } معتمدا في أمورك كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship precedes reliance to indicate that reliance benefits the worshipper.
rows.anchor: وفي تقديم الأمر بعبادة على التوكل تنبيه على أنه إنما ينفع العابد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God emphatically is not unaware of what people do; no threat is more forceful than the fact that He knows their deeds.
rows.anchor: ولا تهديد أبلغ من العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This warning’s substance matches the opening of Hūd, which says the verses were perfected and detailed by the Wise and All-Aware so people worship God alone.
rows.anchor: هذا بعينه مضمون قوله تعالى { كتب أحكمت آياته ثن فصلت من لدن حكيم خبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Raʿd’s aim is to portray revelation as true in itself: sometimes its sound and fame move people toward guidance, while sometimes it instead leaves them blind and astray, like thunder whose lightning and rain may benefit, fail, or harm according to where they fall.
rows.anchor: مقصودها وصف الكتاب بأنه الحق في نفسه ، وتارة يتأثر عنه مع أن له صوتا وصيتا وإرعابا وإرهابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because people differ in how much they know of secrets and how much power guards provide, the passage explains that hidden and open matters are equal to God’s knowledge.
rows.anchor: أتبع ذلك سبحانه بما نفي هذا الاحتمال عنه على وجه الشرح والبيان لاستواء الغيب والشهادة بالنسبة إلى علمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s knowledge is equal regarding whoever conceals speech and whoever declares it.
rows.anchor: سواء منكم } أي في علمه { من أسر القول } أي أخفى معناه في نفسه { ومن جهر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mustakhfin is one who actively seeks concealment, especially at night, believing that hiding can keep divine power from reaching him.
rows.anchor: مستخف } أي موجد الخفاء وطالب له أشد طلب { باليل } في أخفى الأوقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sārib is someone moving quickly toward his purpose across the earth in daylight, openly traversing it.
rows.anchor: سارب } أي ذاهب على وجهه الأرض ومتوجه جار في توجهه إلى قصده بسرعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses iḥtibāk: mentioning the concealed one first implies his counterpart later, and mentioning the traveler later implies his counterpart earlier.
rows.anchor: ذكر { مستخف } أولا دال على ضده ثانيا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the one who has successive guardian angels as either the person hiding or the person traveling openly.
rows.anchor: كما قاله ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما { معقبات } أي أعوان وأنصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muʿaqqibāt are helpers who take turns, each succeeding and replacing another in attending to the person.
rows.anchor: معقبات } أي أعوان وأنصار يتناوبون في أمره بأن يخلف كل واحد منهم صاحبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guarding from front and behind entails guarding both sides; filling every direction around a creature with guardians would be impracticable.
rows.anchor: حفظ جهتي القدام والخلف يستلزم حفظ اليمين والشمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guardians, as the person imagines, protect him from what he fears under God’s encompassing decree.
rows.anchor: يحفظونه } أي في زعمه من كل شيء يخشاه { من أمر الله } أي الذي له الإحاطة الكاملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God changes a people’s good or bad condition only after they change themselves, by exchanging righteous deeds and sound character for corrupt conduct.
rows.anchor: مما كانوا يزينونها به من التحلي بالأعمال الصالحة والتخلي من أخلاق المفسدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even people of great strength cannot prevent harm when God wills it; no one can repel His decree.
rows.anchor: وإذا أراد الله } أي الذي له صفات الكمال { بقوم } أي وإن كانوا في غاية القوة { سوءا فلا مرد له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage denies the people even the least form of protector who could shelter them from God’s action, much less anyone who could rescue or support them like a close ally.
rows.anchor: أتى بصيغة فاعل منقوص إشارة إلى نفي أدنى وجوه الولاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Biqāʿī says he has already given fuller explanation of this verse in al-Anfāl.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم لهذه الآية في الأنفال مزيد بيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God continually shows lightning, a flash like a column of fire, as a sign of His power.
rows.anchor: البرق } وهو لمع كعمود النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lightning is shown to inspire fear because God can make it a deadly thunderbolt; fear is the soul’s alarm at anticipated harm.
rows.anchor: خوفا } أي لأجل إرادة الخوف من قدرته على جعله صواعق مهلكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lightning also arouses hope for beneficial rain; since people do not cause rain to fall, the verse says ṭamaʿ rather than rajāʾ.
rows.anchor: لم يعبر بالرجاء وقال : { وطمعا } أي ولأجل إرادة طمعكم في رحمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, fear and hope can be the intended effects of showing lightning; the showing implies causing fear and hope, which in turn imply that people fear and hope.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى : يريكم ذلك إخافة وإطماعا فتخافون خوفا وتطمعون طمعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, fear and hope may be circumstantial descriptions of the people addressed.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكونا حالين من ضمير المخاطبين أي ذوي خوف وطمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creating means bringing something into being without a producing cause; clouds are collectively named, with a single cloud called saḥābah, and are heavy with water borne on wind.
rows.anchor: والإنشاء : فعل الشيء من غير سبب مولد { السحاب } وهو غيم ينسحب في السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thunder glorifies God by declaring Him free of deficiency and praising His perfect attributes.
rows.anchor: ويسبح الرعد } أي ينزه عن صفات النقص تنزيها ملتبسا { بحمده } أي بوصفه بصفات الكمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says thunder is an angel, but al-Biqāʿī says the report that it is an angel is not sound.
rows.anchor: ويروى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم أن { الرعك ملك } وإن لم يصح أنه ملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even without an authentic angel report, thunder’s glorification shows that its Creator is free of deficiency and possesses every perfection.
rows.anchor: فتسبيحه دلالته على أن موجده سبحانه منزه عن النقص محيط بأوصاف الكمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels also glorify God out of fear of Him.
rows.anchor: { والملائكة } أي تسبح { من خيفته }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lexical excursus links a range of forms to alteration: bodily fatness or change, a tick’s resemblance to a breast, plants and foods that change body or taste, and blood outside its usual condition.
rows.anchor: والصغيرة من القردان أو الضخمة - لشبهها بحلمة الثدي ودود يقع في الجلد قبل الدبغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salt preserves food from corruption and changes flavor or color; because salt signifies rectification, knowledge and other beneficial qualities are metaphorically called salt.
rows.anchor: والملح يصرف المملوح عن الفساد , وأما الماء الملح فمشبه به الطعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Related salt forms describe seasoning a sheep, a sailing wind, disloyalty, angry force, and backbiting, each explained through a change or failure of proper condition.
rows.anchor: وملحه : اغتابه , شبه بمن يتطعم الملح ليعدل مزاجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other related forms name a southern wind, pale varieties of grapes or figs, a kind of report, mixing falsehood with truth, and swelling in a horse’s hock.
rows.anchor: وكذا الملاحي - كفرابي وقد يشدد , وهو عنب أبيض طويل , ونوع من التين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Further senses include a spearhead, a screen, awe that restrains boldness, a great dune or pool that blocks movement, a sea’s depth, and the second winter month’s severe cold.
rows.anchor: والملحة - بالضم : المهابة , لصرفها المجترىء عن قصده ولأن سببها صرف النفس عن هواها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maḥl denotes drought that disrupts the ordinary season by withholding rain and growth; the word also applies to scheming, dust, hardship, and the forceful contest called muḥālah.
rows.anchor: والمحل صرف ما في الزمان عن عادته بعدم المطر والإنبات ورفاهة العيش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author associates further derivatives with abnormal length or form, contrivance, sour milk, a large pulley, a camel’s vertebra, a supporting timber, exhaustion, and changed color.
rows.anchor: وتمحل له : احتال , والممحل - كمعظم - من اللبن : الآخذ طعم حموضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laḥm and related forms refer to the substance or core of things, strengthening or joining a breach, becoming stuck, resemblance, and following or widening a road.
rows.anchor: ولحم الأمر - كمنع : أحكمه , والصائغ الفضة : لأمها , وكذا كل صدع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same joining image explains tightly twisted rope, the Prophet’s battle and its unifying benefit, and a wound knitting together as it heals.
rows.anchor: ونبي الملحمة - من القتال , لأنه ضرب اللحم بالسيف , ومن التأليف كما يكون عن لحمة الثوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sending of Muhammad resembles earlier prophetic missions; like previous messengers, he faces a community that has seen earlier peoples pass away.
rows.anchor: { كذلك } أي مثل إرسال الرسل الذي قدمنا الإشارة إليه في آخر سورة يوسف عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a remarkable mission, and the Prophet has repeatedly been taught that all return and power belong to God, who alone can guide or misguide by a sign or otherwise.
rows.anchor: والذي دربناك عليه غير مرة من أن المرجع إلى الله والكل بيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ummah means a large community of creatures united by a particular distinguishing feature.
rows.anchor: وهي جماعة كثيرة من الحيوان ترجع إلى معنى خاص لها دون غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier communities also endured long hostility, mockery, and demands for a sign from their prophets, persisting in those demands stubbornly even after signs came.
rows.anchor: طال أذاهم لأنبيائهم ومن آمن بهم واستهزاءهم في عدم الإجابة إلى المقترحات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier messengers and their followers kept calling and turned away from mockers as though resigned to the mockers’ demands never being met.
rows.anchor: حتى كأنهم تواصوا بهذا القول حتى فعل الرسل وأتباعهم في إقبالهم على الدعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad was sent to recite what God revealed, especially God’s remembrance, the greatest sign; he should keep reciting despite their disbelief because revelation, not satisfying proposed signs, is the messengers’ task.
rows.anchor: وما ارسلناك ومن قبلك من الرسل إلا لتلاوة ما يوحى , لا لطلب الإجابة إلى ما يقترح الأمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This explanation consoles the Prophet, and the name al-Raḥmān highlights God’s forbearance and long patience toward those who answer kindness and blessing with disbelief.
rows.anchor: وهذا كله تسلية لرسول الله صلىالله عليه وسلم , وقوله : { بالرحمن } إشارة إلى كثرة حلمه وطول أناته
